positioning_categories.description: Vowels with a dominant vertical stem sit to the right of the initial consonant in a side-by-side layout.
positioning_categories.example_breakdown: Initial 'ㄱ' on the left, medial 'ㅏ' on the right.

positioning_categories.description: Vowels with a dominant horizontal stem sit directly underneath the initial consonant in a top-bottom layout.
positioning_categories.example_breakdown: Initial 'ㄱ' on top, medial 'ㅗ' directly underneath.

positioning_categories.description: Compound vowels combining horizontal glides (ㅗ or ㅜ) with vertical vowels wrap around the initial consonant (sitting both below and to its right).
positioning_categories.example_breakdown: Initial 'ㄱ' top-left, horizontal glide 'ㅗ' bottom-left, vertical component 'ㅏ' on the right.

positioning_categories.description: The compound vowel ㅢ combines flat horizontal 'ㅡ' and vertical 'ㅣ'. It visually spans both below and right, but unlike ㅗ/ㅜ-based diphthongs, it derives from a flat non-glide base vowel 'ㅡ'.
positioning_categories.example_breakdown: Initial silent 'ㅇ' top-left, horizontal 'ㅡ' underneath, vertical 'ㅣ' on the right.

batchim_rule.description: Any final consonant (batchim) always sits at the very bottom of the syllable block, below whatever initial+medial structure is above it.
batchim_rule.example_breakdown: Initial 'ㄱ' top-left, medial 'ㅏ' top-right, final batchim 'ㄱ' spanning the bottom.
